NVDA.supply_chain_summary: NVIDIA sits at the apex of the AI compute value chain as a fabless semiconductor designer, critically dependent on TSMC for advanced node manufacturing and HBM memory suppliers (SK Hynix, Micron) for its data center GPU modules. Its downstream is dominated by hyperscalers (Microsoft, Amazon, Google, Meta, Oracle) who collectively account for the majority of data center GPU revenue, creating significant customer concentration risk while reflecting NVIDIA's near-monopoly position in AI accelerator silicon.

AAPL.supply_chain_summary: Apple sits at the center of one of the most complex consumer electronics supply chains in the world, acting as a highly demanding OEM that outsources fabrication to partners like TSMC and assemblers like Foxconn while tightly controlling design and software. On the downstream side, Apple sells primarily through its own retail and online channels, carrier partnerships, and third-party retailers, with its high-margin Services segment increasingly dependent on platform relationships such as the Google search revenue-sharing agreement.

MU.supply_chain_summary: Micron Technology is a vertically integrated memory manufacturer that sits midstream in the semiconductor value chain, purchasing advanced fab equipment and raw materials from capital equipment leaders like ASML, Applied Materials, and Lam Research to produce DRAM and NAND at scale. Its end customers span hyperscale cloud providers, AI accelerator makers, and consumer electronics OEMs, with growing exposure to AI-driven demand for High-Bandwidth Memory making NVIDIA an increasingly critical downstream relationship.

ARM.supply_chain_summary: ARM sits at the apex of the semiconductor intellectual property stack, licensing CPU, GPU, and system IP to virtually every major chip designer globally rather than manufacturing physical products itself, making its downstream licensing relationships with fabless designers and vertically integrated OEMs the core of its business model. Its upstream dependencies are relatively light — primarily EDA software vendors like Cadence and Synopsys for design tooling — while its downstream reach spans mobile, cloud, automotive, and IoT end markets through a broad ecosystem of licensees paying both upfront license fees and per-unit royalties.

MRVL.supply_chain_summary: Marvell Technology is a fabless semiconductor company heavily reliant on TSMC for leading-edge chip manufacturing and ARM/EDA vendors for design IP, with no internal fabrication capacity. Its downstream position is increasingly anchored in AI-driven data center infrastructure, with hyperscalers like AWS, Google, and Microsoft representing a rapidly growing share of revenue through custom ASIC and high-speed networking chip programs.
